623.canonical: Budget for the time cost of mastery learning: it raises examination performance by roughly half a standard deviation and benefits lower-ability or low-aptitude students most (about 0.96 against 0.52 overall), but it increases required instructional time by about 25 per cent — and note that self-paced versions often reduce college completion rates.

664.canonical: Treat the pro-learning-styles evidence base as methodologically unacceptable: the largest favourable syntheses rest mainly on dissertations supervised by their own authors, use attitudinal outcomes and tiny samples, and in at least one case mistook a regression multiple R for the treatment effect size, while the field-level verdict records few studies meeting minimum acceptability criteria, overstatement, poor items and assessments, low validity, negligible impact on practice, and advocacy aimed at commercial ends.

668.canonical: Combine direct instruction with strategy instruction rather than choosing between them, since the two approaches are somewhat independent and models including both produce higher effects than either alone (0.84 combined against 0.72 for either) — including when remediating learning disabilities.

672.canonical: Adopt reciprocal teaching without specialist delivery: it produces d = 0.74 and ordinary classroom teachers achieve the same effect as the study authors, with results not varying by grade level, number of sessions, group size, number of strategies taught, or who did the training, so those implementation choices are free.
